findings.title: Zero SAYT — No Search-As-You-Type
findings.expected_behavior: Real-time autocomplete dropdown showing Livret A, Livret LDDS, Livret Jeune suggestions as user types
findings.actual_behavior: No autocomplete dropdown appeared while typing. Only a 'Effacer ma recherche' clear button appeared. Users must type complete queries and press Enter. Zero SAYT capability confirmed — Inbenta does not provide real-time autocomplete.
findings.impact_stat: +39% conversion rate when sites add real-time search (Co-op with Algolia)
findings.prospect_description: 17M monthly visitors type queries with zero autocomplete guidance. A user typing 'livr' to find their Livret A account sees nothing — no suggestions, no products, no guidance. They either guess the full term or abandon. This is LBP's most visited product category and the most broken entry point.
findings.algolia_solution: Algolia Query Suggestions + InstantSearch provides real-time SAYT with French morphology from the first keystroke. 'livr' immediately surfaces Livret A, Livret LDDS, Livret Jeune results.

findings.title: Partial-Word Search Returns Zero Results
findings.expected_behavior: Prefix matching surfaces Livret A, LDDS, Livret Jeune from the first keystroke on partial input
findings.actual_behavior: Searching 'livr' returns 0 results. Searching full 'livret A' returns 90 results. Search engine requires complete word matches — prefix/partial matching completely absent.
findings.impact_stat: 300-500x faster search and full prefix matching delivered to 250K+ articles at The Times
findings.prospect_description: A customer typing 'livr' — natural abbreviation for 'livret' (LBP's core savings product) — receives zero results. Must know exact product name in full. For a bank serving 10.8M customers including many with lower digital literacy, this is a critical accessibility and inclusion failure.
findings.algolia_solution: Algolia's prefix search handles partial inputs from keystroke 1. 'livr' immediately returns Livret A, Livret LDDS, Livret Jeune with correct French accent handling (epargne = épargne).
findings.algolia_case_study_result: 300-500x faster search, 3.5 hours saved per user per week

findings.title: Semantic NLP Failure — Post Office Appears for Savings Query
findings.expected_behavior: Top results: LEP (3.5% rate), Livret A (1.5% rate), Compte à terme — highest-rate savings products ranked by intent: 'I want the savings product with the best interest rate.'
findings.actual_behavior: Result #5 in solutions: 'Tous les bureaux de Poste — Hartennes et taux' — a post office location page where the town name contains 'taux'. A geographic page appeared in savings product search results because Inbenta keyword-matched 'taux' to the town name Hartennes-et-Taux.
findings.impact_stat: +112% conversions from search at DocMorris after deploying Algolia semantic re-ranking
findings.prospect_description: A customer searching for the savings product with the best rate — a perfectly natural query — receives a post office branch location as a top result. LBP's most commercially critical product category (savings) is being served irrelevant geographic pages. This is the single most damaging finding: Inbenta treats 'taux' as a keyword, not a financial concept.
findings.algolia_solution: Algolia NeuralSearch uses vector embeddings and semantic intent understanding. 'épargne avec le meilleur taux' maps to the savings product category and ranks by interest rate attributes — LEP, Livret A, Compte à terme in the correct order. No geographic pages.

findings.title: Zero Dynamic Facets — No Result Filtering
findings.expected_behavior: Filter panel appears after searching 'assurance' with sub-category options: habitation, auto, santé, vie, prévoyance. Users can narrow by type, price range, coverage level.
findings.actual_behavior: No filter panel on any search results page. Static 8-category navigation on FAQ homepage only. Searching 'assurance' does not expose any sub-category filters.
findings.prospect_description: LBP offers 10+ distinct insurance products (habitation, auto, santé, prévoyance, vie, emprunteur, scolaire). A customer searching 'assurance' gets an undifferentiated list with no ability to filter. They must scroll mixed results or navigate the static menu tree — abandoning search for navigation.
findings.algolia_solution: Algolia Dynamic Faceting automatically generates context-aware filters based on the search query. Searching 'assurance' surfaces facets for product type (habitation/auto/santé), price range, and coverage level — dynamically computed from query context, not statically pre-configured.
findings.algolia_case_study_result: +39% conversion rate, 6% larger basket sizes with Algolia faceting

findings.title: Empty State Shows Zero Discovery Assistance
findings.expected_behavior: Clicking search field displays: popular searches, trending queries (Livret A, assurance habitation, crédit immobilier), recent searches for returning users, curated category shortcuts.
findings.actual_behavior: Clicking search field shows only an empty text box with placeholder 'Rechercher dans la FAQ...' and a Rechercher button. Zero discovery assistance. No popular searches. No trending queries. No recent history.
findings.prospect_description: 17 million monthly visits generate enormous search query data. None of it is surfaced to help new visitors discover what to search for. Users who don't know LBP's product names (e.g., 'LEP' vs 'Livret d'Épargne Populaire') have no guidance whatsoever.
findings.algolia_solution: Algolia Query Suggestions surfaces the top 10 most-searched terms in real time. Empty state becomes an active discovery tool: 'Livret A', 'assurance habitation', 'ouvrir un compte' appear immediately when the search box is activated.
findings.algolia_case_study_result: 300-500x faster search, dramatically improved content discovery across 250K+ articles

findings.title: No Personalization — AB Tasty Present but Disconnected from Search
findings.tested_query: (post-browse of Livret A product page, then broad search)
findings.expected_behavior: After a user browses the Livret A page, subsequent searches show personalized results: related savings products, re-ranked results based on browsing profile.
findings.actual_behavior: No personalized re-ranking after browsing product pages. No 'Recommended for you' sections. AB Tasty (A/B testing) present but data does NOT feed into search ranking. ContentSquare tracks behavior but data does NOT affect search results.
findings.prospect_description: LBP already has AB Tasty and ContentSquare deployed — the behavioral data infrastructure is present. But it is entirely disconnected from search. A customer who spent 5 minutes on the Livret A page gets identical search results as a first-time visitor. The data exists. The connection to search does not.
findings.algolia_solution: Algolia AI Personalization integrates with existing AB Tasty and ContentSquare behavioral signals to re-rank results based on individual user profiles. The data LBP already collects can feed Algolia's personalization engine — no new data collection required.
findings.algolia_case_study_result: +13% additional conversion improvement with Recommend + Search vs. Search alone
